perspective:
**Alice Lim’s available information:**

- I am Alice Lim, a dental hygienist. Austin Moreno is my old friend from high school; we have stayed close and talk about our personal and professional lives. I know Austin works as an insurance agent.
- I noticed Austin had become reserved when work came up. I invited him for coffee and asked if everything was okay at the office.
- I heard Austin say: it was “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs”; then that he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and that it was complicated.
- Because of his reserve and those statements, I believed something specific was bothering him and that he might be hiding something. I did not know what it was.
- I felt worried and wondered whether Austin might be considering a career change due to dissatisfaction at work.
- I suggested a career change/fresh start and mentioned healthcare as an option. I offered to tell him about my experiences and connect him with contacts.
- I heard Austin say he had thought about a change but wasn’t sure what other paths he could take; he asked what I suggested. He said healthcare sounded interesting and he wanted to know more.
- I sensed Austin was hesitant about changing careers because of fear of the unknown. I felt frustration and empathy.
- I told him about my friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and has never been happier.
- I heard Austin say that was inspiring but that he worried about risks and the initial struggle.
- I encouraged him that many people successfully change careers, that growth often comes from stepping out of comfort zones, and that I would support him.
- Austin thanked me and said it helped knowing he had my support and hearing real success stories.
- Seeing his openness, I felt encouraged and hopeful. I suggested he talk to a career counselor and said I had friends in healthcare who could give him a clearer picture.
- I heard Austin say that would be helpful and that he appreciated me helping with connections. I said I would set up a meeting for us next week. He thanked me and said he was looking forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, I believed Austin was ready to take the next steps and appreciated my help. I felt deep satisfaction and joy.
- I told Austin I was proud of the steps he had taken and asked how he felt. He said he felt excited and a bit nervous, but mostly grateful.
- I suggested regular check-ins. He agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that my perspective was good to have.

**I do not know hidden/private facts** such as Austin’s actual job performance, his true unspoken reasons, whether he was hiding something, or his private feelings except as he stated or showed them to me.
